summary: The Thai government is preparing to officially notify Cambodia of its intent to cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims. The proposal is set to be presented to the Cabinet on May 5, 2026. This move comes as Thailand seeks a more modern legal framework for negotiations, though it has sparked warnings from Cambodia regarding regional stability.

Thailand is seeking a new negotiation framework based on international maritime law (UNCLOS) and emphasizes the need for a 'ceasefire in statements' to rebuild trust.

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs is preparing to revoke the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) with Cambodia. Officials intend to shift toward the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to resolve the long-standing 26,000-square-kilometer Overlapping Claims Area (OCA) in the Gulf of Thailand. This strategic move follows Cambodia's recent accession to UNCLOS in February 2026.

summaryTh: กระทรวงการต่างประเทศของไทยเตรียมยกเลิกบันทึกความเข้าใจปี 2544 (MOU 44) กับกัมพูชา โดยเจ้าหน้าที่ตั้งเป้าที่จะเปลี่ยนไปใช้กฎหมายทะเลของสหประชาชาติ (UNCLOS) เพื่อแก้ปัญหาพื้นที่ทับซ้อน 26,000 ตารางกิโลเมตรในอ่าวไทย ความเคลื่อนไหวนี้เกิดขึ้นหลังจากกัมพูชาเพิ่งเข้าเป็นภาคี UNCLOS เมื่อเดือนกุมภาพันธ์ 2569

summary: The Thai government is strengthening cooperation with the US to dismantle major call center networks and human trafficking rings operating along the Thai-Cambodian border. summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow dismissed concerns that Cambodia's alleged registration of MoU 44 before Thailand's official cancellation would harm Thailand's sovereignty over Koh Kut island. He stated that future negotiations will follow the UNCLOS 1982 framework, which clearly shows the island belongs to Thailand. Meanwhile, a military security source revealed that the Thai military has started building a 1.3-kilometer border fence along the frontier in Pong Nam Ron district of Chanthaburi province to enhance safety.

summaryTh: นายสิหศักดิ์ พวงเกตุแก้ว รองนายกรัฐมนตรีและรัฐมนตรีว่าการกระทรวงการต่างประเทศ ปฏิเสธความกังวลที่ว่ากัมพูชาแอบไปจดทะเบียน MoU 2544 ก่อนที่ไทยจะยกเลิกอย่างเป็นทางการ จะส่งผลกระทบต่ออธิปไตยของไทยเหนือเกาะกูด โดยระบุว่าการเจรจาในอนาคตจะดำเนินตามกรอบอนุสัญญาสหประชาชาติว่าด้วยกฎหมายทางทะเล ค.ศ. 1982 (UNCLOS) ซึ่งชี้ชัดว่าเกาะนี้เป็นของไทย ขณะเดียวกัน แหล่งข่าวความมั่นคงเผยว่า กองทัพไทยได้เริ่มสร้างรั้วชายแดนยาว 1.3 กิโลเมตร บริเวณอำเภอโป่งน้ำร้อน จังหวัดจันทบุรี เพื่อเพิ่มความปลอดภัย

summary: The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Military and State Security, Somboon Noonnual, stated that the situation along the Thailand-Cambodia border is currently normal and peaceful. He addressed reports of gunfire from the Cambodian side, characterizing it as an attempt by Cambodia to create a narrative and spin nationalist sentiments, emphasizing that the firing took place strictly within Cambodian territory and did not cross into Thailand. He acknowledged that Thailand's recent cancellation of MOU 44 played a role in inducing Cambodia to adhere more strictly to international frameworks, while confirming that the Thai military remains patient and prepared, including plans to construct border fences in appropriate locations.

summary: Thai security forces, including officers from the Chanthaburi and Trat Border Defence Command, arrested 17 individuals in Pong Nam Ron district of Chanthaburi province for illegal border crossing. The detainees included 13 Cambodian migrant workers without valid travel documents fleeing economic hardship, one Thai driver smuggling them, and two Thai nationals returning from Pailin province, Cambodia. The two Thais admitted to working as administrators for an online gambling operation but fled after Cambodian authorities launched heavy crackdowns on scam networks.

summary: Thai rangers from the 12th Ranger Control Unit in Sa Kaeo province negotiated with Cambodian military personnel after Cambodian villagers brought tractors to prepare farmland in a disputed border area between markers Jor Tor Sor 42 and 44. Thai authorities presented GPS data showing the activity violated MOU 43 by crossing beyond the agreed red-line boundary into territory Thailand considers under its sovereignty. Following the discussion, Cambodian authorities agreed to have the villagers stop their farming activities until the formal border line is officially clarified.

summary: The Thai Senate reviewed a study conducted by an extraordinary committee led by Senator Noppadol Inna regarding the pros and cons of cancelling the 2000 and 2001 MOUs (MOU 43 and MOU 44). The committee unanimously proposed that the government revoke MOU 43, following the previous cabinet decision on May 5 to scrap MOU 44, citing constitutional compliance issues and 26 years of stagnant border demarcation. However, minority senators, including Pornchai Wityalertpan, strongly opposed the move, warning that canceling it without strong justification could allow corporate groups to seize overlapping maritime energy interests and leave Thailand at a disadvantage.

summary: The chairman of the special parliamentary committee on the cancellation of the 2000 and 2001 MOUs briefed 12 foreign ambassadors on Thailand's position. He argued that the agreements have failed to resolve border issues and that Cambodia has repeatedly violated the terms, raising concerns over sovereignty regarding Koh Kood and energy resources.

summary: Cambodian Defense Ministry spokesperson Lt. Gen. Malee Sojiata denied that Cambodian forces fired five shots near Border Marker 18 in Surin province on May 21, calling the Thai army's report 'false information' intended to stir tension. Cambodia reiterated its commitment to the 2025 peace agreements.

title: Cambodia denies allegations of firing 5 shots near Surin border, claims Thailand provides false information

summary: A Senate committee invited ambassadors from ASEAN+3 countries to clarify the rationale behind Thailand's decision to cancel the 2000 and 2001 MOUs regarding border issues. The committee cited concerns that Cambodia has not honored previous agreements and continues to challenge claims regarding Koh Kood.

title: Senate committee briefs ASEAN+3 ambassadors on the government's plan to cancel MOU 2543 and 2544

summary: A Thai Senate committee representative briefed ASEAN+3 diplomats on the rationale for cancelling the 2001 MOU (MOU 43/44) regarding disputed border areas. The committee claims the agreements have failed to progress over 26 years and accuses Cambodia of encroaching on disputed areas and attempting to unilaterally claim petroleum resources.
summaryKh: តំណាងគណៈកម្មាធិការព្រឹទ្ធសភាថៃ បានពន្យល់ដល់ក្រុមការទូតអាស៊ាន+3 អំពីមូលហេតុដែលថៃចង់លុបចោលអនុស្សរណៈយោគយល់គ្នា (MOU) ឆ្នាំ 2001 ទាក់ទងនឹងតំបន់ព្រំដែនដែលមានជម្លោះ ដោយអះអាងថាការចរចាគ្មានវឌ្ឍនភាពអស់រយៈពេល 26 ឆ្នាំមកហើយ។ គណៈកម្មាធិការនេះបានចោទប្រកាន់កម្ពុជាថាបានរំលោភលើតំបន់ដែលមានជម្លោះ និងព្យាយាមទាមទារធនធានប្រេងកាតដោយឯកតោភាគី។
summaryTh: ตัวแทนคณะกรรมาธิการวุฒิสภาไทยชี้แจงต่อคณะทูตอาเซียน+3 ถึงความจำเป็นในการยกเลิก MOU ปี 2544 เกี่ยวกับพื้นที่ทับซ้อน โดยอ้างว่าการเจรจาไม่มีความคืบหน้ามาตลอด 26 ปี พร้อมกล่าวหากัมพูชาว่ารุกล้ำพื้นที่และพยายามอ้างสิทธิแบ่งปันผลประโยชน์ปิโตรเลียมฝ่ายเดียว
title: Senate committee explains why Thailand wants to cancel MOU 43 and MOU 44

summary: Thai troops patrolling near border marker 18 in Kap Choeng district, Surin, reported hearing five gunshots originating from 600 meters away in Cambodian-controlled territory. The Royal Thai Army stated no injuries occurred and no return fire was initiated, but condemned the incident as a violation of the existing ceasefire agreement.

summaryTh: ทหารไทยขณะลาดตระเวนใกล้หลักเขตแดนที่ 18 อ.กาบเชิง จ.สุรินทร์ ได้ยินเสียงปืน 5 นัดจากฝั่งกัมพูชาห่างออกไป 600 เมตร กองทัพบกไทยระบุว่าไม่มีผู้ได้รับบาดเจ็บและไม่ได้ยิงตอบโต้ แต่ประณามว่าการกระทำดังกล่าวเป็นการละเมิดข้อตกลงหยุดยิง

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul discussed the ongoing border tensions between Thailand and Cambodia with French President Emmanuel Macron. He also noted that Cambodia has requested UNESCO to investigate potential damage to World Heritage sites allegedly caused by Thai military actions.
